sentence: The parcels ___ (deliver) every morning before the shop opens.
explanation: Present simple passive (am/is/are + past participle) for regular, repeated actions: are delivered.

sentence: English ___ (speak) as a first language in more than fifty countries.
explanation: Present simple passive: is + spoken. Facts about the language, not about a speaker.

sentence: Passengers ___ (ask) to fasten their seatbelts before take-off.
explanation: Present simple passive: are + asked. The agent (crew) is obvious and omitted.

sentence: These wetlands ___ (threaten) by pollution every single year.
explanation: Present simple passive with the agent introduced by 'by': are threatened by.

sentence: The museum ___ (close) to the public on Mondays.
explanation: Present simple passive: is + closed. No agent needed; the routine is what matters.

sentence: Refunds ___ (not give) without a receipt.
explanation: Negative present simple passive: are not + past participle (given).

sentence: The novel ___ (write) in under three months.
explanation: Past simple passive (was/were + past participle): was written. The writer is not mentioned.

sentence: All the tickets ___ (sell) within an hour of going on sale.
explanation: Past simple passive: were + sold. 'All the tickets' takes a plural verb.

sentence: The ruins ___ (discover) by farmers digging a well in 1923.
explanation: Past simple passive with a expressed agent: were discovered by farmers.

sentence: The decision ___ (announce) at yesterday's press conference.
explanation: 'Yesterday' signals past simple passive: was + announced.

sentence: Thousands of homes ___ (flood) when the river burst its banks.
explanation: Past simple passive: were + flooded. The cause (the river) is in the when-clause.

sentence: The original manuscript ___ (lose) for over a century.
hint: state resulting from a past passive action
explanation: Past simple passive: was + lost. The person who lost it is unknown or unimportant.

sentence: The results ___ (publish) on the university website next Friday.
explanation: Future simple passive: will be + past participle. 'Next Friday' fixes the future reference.

sentence: The new bridge ___ (open) by the mayor next month.
explanation: Future simple passive: will be + opened, with the agent in a by-phrase.

sentence: Your luggage ___ (weigh) at check-in, so allow extra time.
explanation: Future simple passive: will be + weighed. The agent (staff) is obvious.

sentence: The winners ___ (notify) by email at the end of the week.
explanation: Future simple passive: will be + notified for the plural subject 'the winners'.

sentence: The office ___ (repaint) at the moment, so we're working from home.
explanation: Present continuous passive: am/is/are being + past participle. 'At the moment' signals it.

sentence: Historic documents ___ (digitise) right now, which is why the archive is shut.
hint: action in progress now, plural subject
explanation: Present continuous passive: are being + digitised for an action happening around now.

sentence: The finalists ___ (interview) live on air as we speak.
explanation: 'As we speak' demands the present continuous passive: are being + interviewed.

sentence: My usual barber's chair ___ (fix), so I'm trying a new salon.
explanation: Present continuous passive: is being + fixed for an unfinished, ongoing repair.

sentence: The stairs ___ (reinforce) when part of the ceiling gave way.
hint: action in progress at a past moment
explanation: Past continuous passive: was/were being + past participle, interrupted by a sudden past event.

sentence: I couldn't use the meeting room because it ___ (clean) all morning.
explanation: Past continuous passive: was being + cleaned over a period in the past.

sentence: While the sets ___ (build), the actors rehearsed in a warehouse.
hint: two past actions, one passive and ongoing
explanation: Past continuous passive (were being built) for the longer background action.

sentence: The road ___ (resurface) at the time, so we took the coast route instead.
hint: in progress at a past moment
explanation: 'At the time' requires past continuous passive: was being + resurfaced.

sentence: The missing manuscripts ___ (find) — the search is officially over.
explanation: Present perfect passive: have/has been + past participle. The result matters now.

sentence: Every complaint ___ (investigate) since the new ombudsman took over.
explanation: 'Every complaint' is singular, so present perfect passive: has been + investigated.

sentence: Over two hundred bird species ___ (record) in the valley this spring.
explanation: 'This spring' is an open time frame, so present perfect passive: have been + recorded.

sentence: Your booking ___ (confirm) by email — check your spam folder.
explanation: Present perfect passive: has been + confirmed; the confirmation exists now.

sentence: All the passwords ___ (reset) after last week's security breach.
hint: recent past, plural subject, present relevance
explanation: Present perfect passive: have been + reset for a recently completed action.

sentence: By the time the reporters arrived, the evidence ___ (destroy).
explanation: Past perfect passive: had been + past participle for the action completed before the arrival.

sentence: The house looked deserted; it ___ (empty) years earlier.
hint: past event before another past point
explanation: 'Years earlier' is before the past reference point, so past perfect passive: had been + emptied.

sentence: She couldn't pay because her wallet ___ (steal) at the market.
hint: earlier past action causing a past problem
explanation: The theft happened before the failed payment: past perfect passive, had been + stolen.

sentence: The stage was still wet — the scenery ___ (paint) only hours before.
explanation: 'Only hours before' points to the past perfect passive: had been + painted.

sentence: By next June, the entire collection ___ (move) to the new wing.
explanation: Future perfect passive: will have been + past participle for something finished by 'next June'.

sentence: By the time you read this, the treaty ___ (sign) by all twelve delegations.
explanation: 'By the time + present clause' with a future meaning takes the future perfect passive.

sentence: By Friday afternoon, every application ___ (process).
explanation: 'By + future time' signals future perfect passive: will have been + processed.

sentence: This form ___ (sign) in ink — digital signatures aren't valid.
explanation: Modal passive: modal + be + past participle. Obligation: must (also has to) be signed.

sentence: Your name ___ (find) anywhere on the guest list, I'm afraid.
explanation: Modal passive of ability/possibility: cannot be + past participle.

sentence: Parcels ___ (leave) in the porch if nobody is home.
explanation: Modal passive: should be + left. A recommendation; 'are left' (routine) is also acceptable.

sentence: The debt ___ (repay) in full by May, he promised.
explanation: Reported future passive: would be + past participle after a past reporting verb.

sentence: The match ___ (abandon) because of the storm, so we got a refund.
explanation: Modal passive with have to: had to be + past participle for past obligation.

sentence: The markings ___ (see) with the naked eye.
explanation: Modal passive: cannot be + seen. The context (astronomy) implies impossibility.

sentence: Endangered plants ___ (not pick) anywhere in the reserve.
explanation: Modal passive of prohibition: must not be + past participle.

sentence: The whole engine ___ (strip down) before the fault could be located.
explanation: Past necessity: had to be + stripped down (phrasal verbs passivise too, particle retained).

sentence: The rare print ___ (steal) from the locked cabinet — the lock wasn't forced.
explanation: Perfect modal passive: must have been + past participle for a confident past deduction.

sentence: The invitation ___ (send) to the wrong address — nobody on this street received one.
explanation: Perfect modal passive: must have been + sent. The evidence forces the conclusion.

sentence: This wall ___ (build) centuries ago — no modern tool leaves marks like these.
explanation: Perfect modal passive: must have been + built to draw a conclusion about the past.

sentence: The village ___ (reach) by road until 1962; only mules could make the climb.
explanation: 'Until 1962' describes a past state of affairs: could not be + past participle.

sentence: The manuscript is too fragile ___ (handle) without gloves.
explanation: Passive to-infinitive: to be + past participle. The manuscript receives the handling.

sentence: Several issues remain ___ (resolve) before the launch.
explanation: 'Remain' + passive infinitive (to be resolved) expresses unfinished business.

sentence: She hates ___ (interrupt) when she's deep in work.
explanation: Passive gerund: being + past participle, after verbs like hate, like, avoid.

sentence: He refuses ___ (tell) what to do by people he's never met.
explanation: 'Refuse' takes a to-infinitive; passive meaning needs to be + told.

sentence: There's still a lot of paperwork ___ (complete) before we can close the account.
explanation: Noun + passive to-infinitive (paperwork to be completed) — the paperwork receives the action.

sentence: The escaped prisoner ___ (believe) to be hiding in the mountains.
explanation: Impersonal passive pattern: subject + is believed/said/reported + to-infinitive.

sentence: The company ___ (say) to be on the verge of bankruptcy.
explanation: It is said that... → The company is said to be... Present simple passive: is said.

sentence: The two leaders ___ (report) to have reached a provisional agreement.
explanation: Plural subject needs are: are reported to have reached (perfect infinitive for the earlier event).

sentence: She ___ (think) to be the finest violinist of her generation.
explanation: Impersonal passive: is thought to be. The thinkers are general, not stated.

sentence: The divers ___ (know) to have been working without insurance.
explanation: are known to have been working: the knowing is present, the working was ongoing before.

sentence: The temple is thought ___ (build) more than two thousand years ago.
explanation: Perfect passive infinitive: to have been + built for an event earlier than the main verb.

sentence: The painting is believed ___ (steal) by an organised gang.
explanation: The theft preceded the believing: is believed to have been + stolen.

sentence: The Eiffel Tower ___ (design) by Gustave Eiffel's engineering firm.
explanation: Past simple passive with agent: was designed by. Historical events take past simple.

sentence: The national anthem ___ (compose) by a little-known music teacher.
explanation: Past simple passive: was + composed; 'by a music teacher' names the agent.

sentence: The ambush ___ (plan) by someone with intimate knowledge of the valley.
explanation: Past perfect passive (had been planned) stresses completion before the ambush; was planned is also acceptable.

sentence: Hamlet ___ (perform) almost continuously since it was written.
explanation: 'Since + past clause' requires present perfect passive: has been + performed.

sentence: We're having the kitchen ___ (renovate) next month.
explanation: Causative 'have something done': have + object + past participle. Professionals do it for us.

sentence: She had her laptop ___ (repair) after the coffee spill.
explanation: Causative structure: had + her laptop + repaired. A technician performed the repair.

sentence: You should get that rash ___ (look at) by a doctor.
explanation: Causative 'get something done': get + object + past participle (looked at).

sentence: I must get my passport ___ (renew) before the trip.
explanation: 'Get + object + past participle': the passport is renewed by an authority, not by me.

sentence: They're getting the garden ___ (landscape) this spring.
explanation: Causative with get: are getting + the garden + landscaped.

sentence: He had his wisdom tooth ___ (take out) yesterday morning.
explanation: Causative: had + his wisdom tooth + taken out. The particle 'out' stays with the participle.

sentence: We had the whole house ___ (repaint) before the wedding.
explanation: 'Had the house repainted' — painters did it at our request. Object + past participle.

sentence: Did you have the brakes ___ (check) before the long drive?
hint: question form of have something done
explanation: Causative question: Did you have + the brakes + checked? A mechanic did the checking.

sentence: The experiments ___ (conduct) under strict laboratory conditions last year.
explanation: 'Last year' fixes past simple passive: were + conducted for the plural subject.

sentence: A new ring road ___ (construct) around the city at present.
explanation: 'At present' requires present continuous passive: is being + constructed.

sentence: The refugees ___ (provide) with blankets and hot meals last night.
explanation: Past simple passive: were + provided. Note the pattern provide somebody WITH something.

sentence: Too much time ___ (waste) on pointless meetings these days.
explanation: 'These days' signals a present general situation: is + wasted (singular 'time').

sentence: The old cinema ___ (demolish) last month.
explanation: Past simple passive: was + demolished. The demolition company is not mentioned.

sentence: Her memoir ___ (translate) into fourteen languages so far.
explanation: 'So far' requires present perfect passive: has been + translated (singular 'memoir').

sentence: The stolen car ___ (find) abandoned in a car park this morning.
explanation: 'This morning' (now over) takes past simple passive: was + found.

sentence: All new students ___ (give) a locker key on their first day.
explanation: Present simple passive: are + given. Passives of give keep the indirect object as subject.

sentence: The bridge ___ (inspect) twice a year for signs of corrosion.
explanation: 'Twice a year' marks a routine: present simple passive, is + inspected.

sentence: Construction ___ (halt) after the discovery of Roman remains.
explanation: Past simple passive: was + halted. The halting authority is unnamed.

sentence: The recipe ___ (pass down) from generation to generation.
hint: continuing relevance from past to now
explanation: Present perfect passive: has been + passed down; the process links past and present.

sentence: My laptop ___ (service) next week, so back up your files beforehand.
explanation: 'Next week' takes the future passive: will be + serviced (is being serviced is also a valid arrangement).

sentence: The castle ___ (restore) at present, so the east wing is closed to visitors.
explanation: Present continuous passive: is being + restored for work in progress now.

sentence: The new stadium ___ by the end of the decade.
explanation: 'By the end of the decade' needs future perfect passive: will have been + completed. The stadium is completed by somebody.

sentence: A decision ___ once all the evidence has been reviewed.
explanation: The decision cannot make itself: future passive will be + made.

sentence: The suspect is believed ___ the country weeks ago.
explanation: Believe + to-infinitive; 'weeks ago' demands the perfect infinitive to have left.

sentence: The tickets ___ at the door from seven o'clock.
explanation: Modal passive: can be + collected. The tickets are collected by the buyers.

sentence: These wires must ___ by a qualified electrician.
explanation: After a modal, passive = be + past participle: must be checked. 'Been' needs 'have'.

sentence: The ancient scrolls are far too brittle ___ .
explanation: The scrolls receive the action: passive infinitive to be + unrolled.

sentence: By this time tomorrow, the results ___ to every candidate.
explanation: 'By this time tomorrow' requires future perfect passive: will have been + emailed.

sentence: She's having her wedding dress ___ by a tailor in Naples.
explanation: Have + object + past participle: having her dress made by a professional.

sentence: I don't like ___ how to run my own department.
explanation: The speaker receives the telling: passive gerund being + told.

sentence: The fault ___ by the time the auditor arrived.
explanation: The fixing preceded the arrival: past perfect passive had been + fixed.

sentence: A cheaper version of the vaccine ___ right now.
explanation: 'Right now' requires present continuous passive: is being + developed.

sentence: The report must ___ before Friday's board meeting.
explanation: Modal passive: must be + submitted. 'Been' would require have (must have been submitted).

sentence: The letters ___ while the family was on holiday.
explanation: Ongoing during the holiday: past continuous passive were being + opened.

sentence: The manuscript is said ___ in a private vault for decades.
explanation: 'For decades' before now: perfect passive infinitive to have been + kept.

sentence: The theatre ___ in 1897 and reopened last year.
explanation: A finished date (1897) takes past simple passive: was + built.

sentence: Guests ___ to arrive no later than seven.
explanation: Guests receive the request: present simple passive are + asked.

sentence: Your contract will ___ for a further twelve months.
explanation: After 'will', passive = be + past participle: will be renewed.

sentence: The evidence ___ by an independent laboratory at present.
explanation: 'At present' needs present continuous passive: is being + analysed. The lab does the analysing.

sentence: The whole street ___ when the gas main burst.
explanation: The street was evacuated by others: past necessity had to be + evacuated.

sentence: I need this report ___ by noon, not five.
explanation: Need + object + past participle: the report is typed by somebody else (causative-like).

sentence: The winners ___ a trophy at the closing ceremony.
hint: passive of a verb with two objects
explanation: Give somebody something → somebody is given something: future passive will be + given.

sentence: The matter ___ at this very moment, so no comment yet.
explanation: Look into (investigate) passivises with the particle kept: is being looked into.

sentence: The manuscript might ___ if you keep touching it with bare hands.
explanation: Get + past participle (get damaged) is an informal passive common with mishaps.

sentence: Nothing ___ about the incident until the inquiry began.
explanation: Nothing was known by anybody: past simple passive was + known.

sentence: He's getting his eyes ___ next week.
explanation: Causative get + object + past participle: getting his eyes tested (by an optician).

sentence: The message ___ have been misheard by the interpreter.
explanation: Perfect modal passive = modal + have been + past participle: must have been misheard.

sentence: The road ___ at the moment — use the bypass.
explanation: 'At the moment' — present continuous passive: is being repaired.

sentence: The castle ___ in the twelfth century.
explanation: A completed past date takes the past simple passive.

sentence: The letters ___ by the time I arrived at the office.
explanation: Past perfect passive: the sending preceded the arrival.

sentence: The suspect ___ to have left the country.
explanation: 'People believe' → 'is believed to have left'.

sentence: A new policy ___ next month.
explanation: The policy receives the action: 'will be introduced'.

sentence: The house ___ badly since the owner emigrated.
explanation: 'Since' + present perfect passive.

sentence: The results ___ tomorrow at noon.
explanation: The results receive the action: 'will be announced'.

sentence: The bridge ___ by a locally trained architect.
explanation: 'Was designed by' — passive with the agent in a by-phrase.

sentence: Nothing ___ about the leak until the inspector came.
explanation: 'Nothing was said' — the passive of 'nobody said'.

sentence: The passengers ___ to fasten their seatbelts as the plane entered the storm.
explanation: 'The passengers were told to …' — passive of 'tell somebody to do'.

sentence: This bridge ___ repaired twice this year already.
explanation: 'Already' + present perfect passive: has been repaired.

sentence: He ___ to be the best chef in the region.
explanation: 'People think he is …' → 'he is thought to be …'.
